nodes.label: supermux
nodes.rationale: Open-source mobile-first agentic development environment: run Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and OpenCode on hardware you control, then steer, review, and merge from anywhere. No supermux account required.

nodes.label: supermux broker
nodes.rationale: The broker is the source of truth on the host: supervises agent sessions, keeps histories, routes messages, exposes workspace APIs. Control operations happen in the broker so switching or inspecting sessions does not spend agent tokens.

nodes.label: Pairing not accounts
nodes.rationale: New devices join with a short-lived single-use claim bound to the host identity. A client can keep several independently owned hosts in one fleet.

nodes.label: Connectivity relay
nodes.rationale: Native CLI and desktop hosts enable the built-in relay by default for a stable HTTPS address without opening a router port. Relay connections are encrypted in transit but not yet end-to-end encrypted at the application layer.

nodes.label: Git worktree isolation
nodes.rationale: Every worker is isolated in its own git worktree. The main checkout moves only through the finish action the user chooses.

nodes.label: Personal assistant sessions
nodes.rationale: Optional always-on orchestrators created from Settings; fresh installs do not create one.

nodes.label: Local-first trust boundary
nodes.rationale: Repositories, credentials, session history, and broker state remain on the host. Clients can connect over LAN, VPN, reverse proxy, or tunnel.
